mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% mean) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 6% within a month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% mean) when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and suppresses earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% mean) during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-mo average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% mean) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong month-over-month increase in personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) combined with a flat or declining housing starts index (HOUST) suggests a shift from durable goods to services consumption, which historically correlates with lower cyclically sensitive equity outperformance, resulting in muted S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >0.3% m/m and HOUST does not rise m/m
failure_condition: S&P 500 20d forward returns are not statistically indistinguishable from zero when PAYEMS rises >0.3% and HOUST is flat or falling.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the participation rate (implied by UNRATE dynamics and PAYEMS) above 63% for three consecutive months signals a tighter labor market, which supports wage growth and corporate margin pressure, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as markets anticipate earnings upgrades.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and implied participation rate > 63% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5d forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.5% mean) when participation rate exceeds 63% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS outpacing PAYEMS) for two consecutive quarters indicates households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which typically precedes a consumer spending rebound and supports future earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS grows faster than PAYEMS for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60d forward returns are not significantly positive (>1% mean) when RSAFS outpaces PAYEMS for two consecutive quarters.
